items.title: Bessent Faces G20 Credibility Test Amid Interventions
items.content: <article>US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent’s interventionist summer has already led to pushback and questions about his credibility in financial markets. Now he faces a test with global peers.  Ahead of the meeting of Group of 20 finance ministers in Asheville, North Carolina, on Monday, Bessent has vowed to return the conversation among the world’s top economic policymakers to the core subject of boosting growth. The challenge for Bessent in selling this message is that the biggest threats to global growth this year have come from the high energy prices and other consequences of President Donald Trump’s war on Iran, as well as the impact of US tariffs that are again in focus with the launch of a new trade war against fellow G20 member Canada.  Bloomberg Senior Economics Writer Shawn Donnan joins Bloomberg Businessweek Daily to discuss. He speaks with Tim Stenovec and Kristine Aquino. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Ares Raises $3.8 Billion for Japan-Focused Logistics Fund
items.author: Megawati Wijaya
items.content: <article>Ares Management Corp has raised ¥612 billion ($3.8 billion) for its latest Japan-focused logistics development fund, in the largest closed-end institutional fundraise by its real estate business.</article>

items.title: Apple’s Ternus Takes the CEO Reins
items.content: <article>Stepping into his new role as Apple's chief executive officer on Sept. 1, John Ternus won’t have much time before the company begins its annual fall product rollouts. This year the lineup will include an unusually ambitious slate of devices he’s been teasing for months internally, including the first foldable iPhone and a smart display that can recognize who’s speaking and tailor content to them. Bloomberg News Managing Editor for Consumers Tech Mark Gurman reports on what's next for Apple. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Asian Stocks to Fall as Iran Flare-Up Boosts Oil: Markets Wrap
items.author: Rob Verdonck
items.content: <article>Stocks in Asia are set to follow Wall Street lower as renewed geopolitical tensions lifted oil prices, reviving inflation concerns and the prospect of further monetary tightening.</article>

items.title: Latest Oil Market News and Analysis for Sept. 1
items.author: Kanoko Matsuyama and Mia Gindis
items.content: <article>Oil pushed higher after the biggest gain in three weeks on Monday as fresh hostilities between the US and Iran raised concerns about prolonged disruptions to energy flows through the Strait of Hormuz.</article>

items.title: Japan Bonds Face Test at 10-Year Sale as Yield Approaches 3%
items.author: Mia Glass
items.content: <article>Japan’s auction of 10-year government bonds on Tuesday will test demand for this key maturity as yields approach the milestone of 3% and investors position for an interest rate hike from the central bank.</article>

items.title: Australia Raises Wheat Crop Forecast as Export Demand Picks Up
items.author: Ben Westcott
items.content: <article>Australia raised its wheat crop forecast after strong winter rains improved growing conditions, just as the worsening Black Sea crisis creates additional demand for the country’s grain.</article>

items.title: Hedge Fund Disclosure Deadline Delayed Again by SEC, CFTC
items.author: Lydia Beyoud
items.content: <article>US regulators delayed for the fourth time additional hedge fund disclosure requirements that are meant to inform agencies about the financial positions of firms during market turbulence.</article>

items.title: ETFs Are an Engine of Growth, Says T. Rowe Price’s Sawyer
items.content: <article>Dee Sawyer, head of global distribution at T. Rowe Price says ETFs are an engine of growth for the firm. She also talks about the acquisition of upstart ETF provider F/m Investments. She said the deal improves their investment capability. She speaks on "Bloomberg The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Brookfield Lines Up a $600 Million Payout in Niche Credit Market
items.author: Paula Seligson and Scott Carpenter
items.content: <article>HomeServe is in early discussions with lenders for an asset-backed transaction that would pay owner Brookfield Asset Management Ltd. a dividend of $600 million, according to people with knowledge of the matter.</article>

items.title: Refiners Granted Highest Level of Biofuel Waivers Since 2017
items.author: Elizabeth Elkin and Cole Martin
items.content: <article>The Trump administration granted smaller oil refineries the biggest amount of exemptions from mandates requiring them to blend renewable fuels since 2017.</article>

items.title: Dollar Weakens for a Second Month on Treasury Buyback
items.author: Anya Andrianova
items.content: <article>The dollar declined for a second straight month as US plans to accelerate buyback of government debt weighed on the greenback.</article>

items.title: S&P 500 Slips as Oil Spike, Rising Fed Rate Bets Pressure Stocks
items.author: Jessica Menton
items.content: <article>US stocks slumped on Monday, with escalating Middle East tensions and rising oil prices weighing on sentiment as traders boosted bets on interest-rate hikes this year.</article>

items.title: Treasury Market Selloff Sends 10-Year Yield to 19-Month High
items.author: Elizabeth Stanton
items.content: <article>The US 10-year yield topped 4.75% on Monday for the first time since January 2025 as rising oil prices bolstered expectations that the Federal Reserve will hike interest rates.</article>

items.title: Strategy Restarts Bitcoin Buying, Spending $370 Million
items.author: David Pan
items.content: <article>Strategy Inc. resumed Bitcoin purchases after a 10-week pause, returning to its signature accumulation strategy after the crypto bear market pressured its shares, weakened confidence in the financing model and prompted a balance-sheet overhaul.</article>

items.title: War, Weather Push Crop Prices to Biggest Monthly Gain Since 2012
items.author: Eleanor Thornber and Ben Westcott
items.content: <article>Crop prices capped their biggest monthly jump in more than a decade as wars and extreme weather disrupt supplies, raising concerns about food inflation.</article>

items.title: EM Stocks See Best August Run Since 2004, FX Posts Monthly Gain
items.author: Srinivasan Sivabalan, Prima Wirayani and Beatriz Amat
items.content: <article>Emerging-market stocks posted their biggest August advance since 2004 as a rally broadened beyond the biggest artificial-intelligence stocks and got a boost from commodities.</article>

items.title: Gold Slips as Renewed Mideast Tensions Keep Fed Hike Bets Alive
items.author: Yihui Xie and Yvonne Yue Li
items.content: <article>Gold edged down as renewed geopolitical risks stoked concerns about inflationary pressures that could make the Federal Reserve hike interest rates, a headwind for the precious metal.</article>

items.title: Stocks Fall as US-Iran Strikes Spur Rally in Oil: Markets Wrap
items.author: Rita Nazareth
items.content: <article>A flare-up in geopolitical risks sent stocks and bonds lower as oil climbed, raising concerns about inflationary pressures that could make the Federal Reserve raise interest rates.</article>

items.title: Latest Oil Market News and Analysis for Aug. 31
items.author: Mia Gindis, Charles Gorrivan and Paul Burkhardt
items.content: <article>Oil rose the most in three weeks as tensions spiked in the Middle East, with the US and Iran exchanging strikes for the first time in about a month and fighting appearing poised to continue.</article>
